identity.description: Innovations state-space exponential smoothing: recursively weighted level, trend, and seasonal components with exponentially decaying memory. The workhorse mid-tier forecaster — more robust than ARIMA on short business series, strictly stronger than the naive floors when trend or seasonality is real.

consumes.note: single regular time-indexed numeric series; multiplicative trend/seasonal variants additionally require strictly positive values

emits.note: point forecast over the horizon; prediction intervals are native in the state-space ETSModel form — the legacy holtwinters.ExponentialSmoothing is point-only (simulate() for intervals). Driver targets ETSModel for this reason.
smoothing parameters (alpha/beta/gamma), damping phi, and initial states; standard errors only in the ETSModel state-space form

trend.note: trend component form; 'mul' requires a strictly positive series

damped_trend.note: damping flattens long-horizon trend extrapolation — usually the safer choice for business series

seasonal_periods.note: the cycle length s; gated by n_full_cycles like every seasonal order in this family

smoothing_level.note: alpha — normally left null so the optimizer fits it by max likelihood; exposed for pinning only

invariances.why: level/trend/seasonal recursions are equivariant to rescaling the series; forecasts and intervals rescale with it
a log transform converts multiplicative structure to additive — it changes WHICH ETS variant is correct, so it is a modeling choice, not a no-op
the smoothing recursion consumes every consecutive step; gaps break the state update and must be interpolated to a regular grid first
operates on a single numeric series; there is no exogenous-regressor pathway at all (unlike SARIMAX)
the innovations state-space form assumes Gaussian single-source-of-error innovations for valid prediction intervals; point forecasts need much less

seasonal ETS needs >=2 full cycles to identify the seasonal states, but tolerates shorter history than ARIMA at equal orders — validated on real dues data where ETS reached MASE 1.84 vs seasonal-naive 2.08
trend extrapolation is explicit and linear (or damped) in the state equations — damping exists precisely because undamped trend extrapolation overshoots long horizons

featureStats.why: decides whether the seasonal component (gamma recursion) is warranted; near-zero strength means seasonal ETS just fits noise into the seasonal states
a persistent trend selects the beta recursion and flags damped vs undamped — the single biggest driver of long-horizon ETS error
family gate: fewer than 2 complete cycles makes the seasonal states unidentifiable — drop to non-seasonal ETS or the naive floor
multiplicative trend/seasonal variants are only defined on strictly positive series — this stat prunes half the ETS variant space up front

modelMetrics.why: the family's honest scoreboard; empirical anchor: on real association dues data ETS scored MASE 1.84 against the seasonal-naive floor's 2.08 — a genuine, modest beat, which is what real membership series look like

edgeCases.condition: non-positive values with multiplicative trend or seasonal
edgeCases.behavior: fit raises or produces NaN states
edgeCases.note: restrict to additive variants or log-shift first

edgeCases.behavior: degenerate zero-variance fit; optimizer may not converge

edgeCases.condition: optimizer non-convergence on flat noisy series
edgeCases.behavior: smoothing params pinned at bounds (alpha near 0 or 1)
edgeCases.note: bound-pinned alpha is a diagnosable symptom — refit simpler variant

driver.constructor: ETSModel(endog, error='add', trend=, damped_trend=, seasonal=, seasonal_periods=).fit()
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col, freq, horizon); predict becomes get_prediction(horizon) for intervals; variant pruning by positivity check

placementClaims.why: the recursion needs a gap-free regular grid; time-aware interpolation, never tabular median
log transform converts multiplicative seasonality to additive, collapsing the variant search and stabilizing variance
scale-equivariant recursions; standardization changes nothing about the fit
single numeric series — nothing to encode and no exogenous pathway
